record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the eighth international conference on fuzzy set theory and applications
record.original_question: An interval semigroup is a linearly ordered semigroup S = ([0, 1], *, <=) with 0 as annihilator and no neutral element, considered here in the continuous Archimedean case. A non-decreasing mapping f: [0, 1] -> R is a multiplicative generator of S when x * y = f^(-1)(f(x) * f(y)) for all x, y in [0, 1], where f^(-1) denotes the pseudo-inverse of f. Which nilpotent interval semigroups admit a continuous multiplicative generator?

evidence.quote: Such an algebraic structure will be called an interval semigroup: in the sequel, it is intended that S is a continuous Archimedean interval semigroup.
We say that a non-decreasing mapping f : I -> R is a multiplicative generator of S if x * y = f^(-1)(f(x) * f(y)) for all x, y in I.
Problem 5.2. Characterize the nilpotent interval semigroups which admit a continuous multiplicative generator.

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive characterization or a paper explicitly resolving the question of which nilpotent continuous Archimedean interval semigroups admit a continuous multiplicative generator. Related literature on additive and multiplicative generators of continuous Archimedean t-norms exists (Aczél, Faucett, and standard t-norm references), but no source clearly settling this specific characterization problem was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses multiplicative generators in the context of continuous Archimedean t-norms but does not provide a characterization of nilpotent interval semigroups admitting continuous multiplicative generators.
status_evidence.claim: Standard expositions cover multiplicative generators of t-norms without resolving this characterization.
